answer: A durable proof of attention has to bind three things at once: the umber moment when someone actually looks, the jade trace that the look leaves behind, and the river record that lets anyone else check it later. If any one of the three is missing, the proof collapses into a claim, and claims are cheap to fake at scale. The check must be tied to a single human, verified across sessions, so a duplicate cannot replay the same evidence under a second name.
